author: bshastry
content: Hello! I hope this is the right channel to report such an issue. Grandine caches (without an upper bound) invalid signed envelopes (don't need to be builder) with slot = u64::MAX, so it is possible to DoS a Grandine node via gossip. One vector is millions of zero-byte txs in the signed envelope.

author: m.kalinin
content: Q: with ePBS, what is the publishing strategy for blobs? Publish at the same time as the payload or earlier/later?

author: potuz
content: I don't know what builders will do but the honest strategy is to publish as soon as you see the block including your bid

author: nc1234
content: not only honest, but probably incentivized to publish as soon as you see your bid in the block to get DA votes from ptc.

author: christoph7800
content: Hi there, I was looking at the current Gloas specs. Are `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS` and `PAYLOAD_ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS` at 6s and 9s respectively what is currently expected to ship? Put differently, is the free option going to remain in the protocol without a protocol-level mitigation?

author: potuz
content: Yes as of now, I believe the strongest mitigation we have for the free option problem is a first-offense global ban of any relay  and all builders participating in that relay. Other than that we have nothing better than penalties but those are not in protocol as of now.

author: krisoshea.eth
content:
Hey everyone. I'm working on the Lodestar EIP-7732 builder with <@921369499733725205> as part of the EPF, mentored by <@586161934425128960> and <@1035747431461167125>.

I recently opened https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/641, which adds builder_index and block_hash to the block SSE event from Gloas onwards. Today a sidecar builder has to fetch every imported block to find out whether it includes its bid; with these two fields it can tell from the event itself. The PR also links an alternative patch that adds a separate bid_included event and leaves the block event unchanged.

In the review, <@737740104281489531> suggested a different approach that I think is definitely worth discussing here. Instead of telling the builder its bid was included, the beacon node would send a "reveal now" event once the block has enough attestation weight behind it (40% was floated, configurable), and send nothing if the block doesn't get there before the payload deadline.

My view, which I've set out on the PR, is that the inclusion fields should land either way, because they're information the node already has at import time. A reveal signal is a policy decision, and the node doesn't currently have the data to make it well, for three reasons:

author: krisoshea.eth
content:
- Fork choice doesn't count attestations for the current slot, so the node would need a new live tally of gossip attestations.
- Before aggregates arrive, a node only sees attestations on the subnets it subscribes to, and aggregates are due at 50% of the slot, the same moment the payload is due. So the same threshold would mean different things on different nodes.
- If the event doesn't fire but the block still reaches the 60% payment quorum on chain, the builder pays the bid without having revealed. That's the worst outcome a builder can have.

Consequently, I have three questions for everyone involved here:

1. Extended block event or a separate bid_included event: which is easier to implement and adopt?
2. Could a beacon node produce a meaningful attestation-weight signal before PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS, and if so, what should it be measured against? The spec's payment quorum uses total active balance divided by SLOTS_PER_EPOCH.
3. Does a reveal hint belong in the beacon API at all, or should it stay builder-side policy built on the block event, head_v2 and the builder's own clock?

Cheers!

author: potuz
content: wait does the builder really need to be speced? Why would we need to standardize an event that every beacon needs to serve  when the only consumer is a builder that other clients may want to code in a different way?

author: potuz
content: not that I have anything really against this, it may be useful for prysm's too, but I have been feeling for years that the overspecification in ethereum has going through the roof
